w uses floor division, so a window covers `[start, start+Size)`: an instant belongs to the window that has already started, and an instant exactly on a boundary starts the next window:

```go
return unix - ((unix%Size)+Size)%Size
```

(The `+Size` term keeps the remainder non-negative for negative timestamps, so floor division holds for all inputs, not just non-negative unix seconds.) Nothing else in the pipeline (parsing, sink/rollup, formatting) changed.

## Verification

- **`go test ./...` passes** — fresh `-count=1` run: 185 packages ok, 0 failures.

The event at `119` stays in `t=60` instead of leaking into `t=120`, and the boundary events at `60`/`120` start their own windows.

## Fix

```go
// Windows are half-open: an instant exactly on a boundary starts a new
// window (see docs/pipeline.md). So a window [start, start+Size) owns the
// instants start <= t < start+Size, and Start is floor division by Size.
func Start(unix int64) int64 {
	return (unix / Size) * Size
}
```

This implements `[start, start+width)` exactly: `59 → 0`, `60 → 60`, `119 → 60`, `120 → 120`.
